spiritual_reading: This text resists translation because its natural sense is too fragmentary to determine stable functions for most terms and actions. What can be drawn from what remains is this: a complete cycle of spiritual ordering was being commanded for all things under a single governance, so that they would be brought into a sufficient state for conjunction. Then a particular recipient was also brought into view, and at the appointed state of readiness the influx of wisdom was opened to him, so that the whole domain of knowledges and their connections could be made manifest in his understanding. He was then to be turned entirely toward that wisdom, to live from it as his ruling principle. Finally, it indicates that this state and power did not arise from his own proprium, but was distinguished from three other discrete degrees within him, which stand beneath and must receive in their order what descends from the higher.

fills.notes: The fragment begins with “all of them”, and the spiritual context speaks of a complete ordering under a single governance. In the oldest Iranian substrate this is normally expressed as the collective of primary Light-powers (aeons) being brought into order before a work of conjunction.
The spiritual sense indicates an ordering being commanded for all things. The natural-layer verb expected here is a directive act establishing order, not exhortation.
Matches the stated aim: brought into a sufficient state for conjunction. Old substrate phrasing tends to be impersonal: readiness, fitting, establishing.

The “seven people” in Manichaean-Coptic dress usually covers the seven luminaries or seven ruling powers; in the oldest cosmological register they belong to the Light-order rather than a moral or ecclesial group.
The spiritual context requires an “appointed state of readiness” at which influx is opened. In the cosmological idiom, that appointed completion is expressed as fullness or completion of the time.
The phrase “of the light …” is followed by an opening to disclosure and manifestation. In correspondential terms this is influx of wisdom from Light; thus the Light is qualified by its wisdom.
The spiritual sense: “the whole domain of knowledges and their connections could be made manifest.” The natural-layer counterpart is the universe with its orders, ranks, or arrangements.
The disclosure is specifically into the understanding of the particular recipient brought into view; the natural text likely marked the dative recipient at the point “is revealed …”.
The surviving “utt]erly” demands an intensifier completing a word like “wholly, utterly”. This matches the spiritual requirement: turned entirely toward wisdom.

“the way that he exists … from …” in the spiritual reading is living from that wisdom as the ruling principle. The natural layer commonly expresses this as existing ‘in it’ (in the Light, in Wisdom) rather than from self.
Directly required by the spiritual sense: the state and power are not from the proprium. The oldest layer states this as an impersonal negation of self-origin.

The closing contrasts “these other three” with what is above them. The spiritual sense specifies three discrete degrees beneath which must receive in order. Thus the missing phrase names them as degrees, not persons or rules.

assessment: Much of the chapter is too broken for verbatim recovery, but the correspondential structure is tight: an initial ordering of the Light-powers, an appointed fullness of time, opening of Light-wisdom revealing the ordered universe to a recipient, an injunction to turn wholly to that wisdom, and a final denial of self-origin contrasted with three lower discrete degrees. Several fills remain moderate because the exact Coptic lexeme cannot be fixed from the fragment, but the required cosmological functions are strongly constrained.
